questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".

My father is in (a teaching profession).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**the profession of teaching**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• While '**teaching**' alone could be used, the phrase "**the profession of teaching**" provides a more formal and complete expression, indicating the teaching career as a whole, which works better in some formal contexts.
 
• The use of '**the**' before '**profession**' is suitable because it denotes a specific profession that is already implied in the statement - in this case, teaching.
 
• So, the correct sentence should be "*My father is in **the profession of teaching**.*"

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• '**Teaching**': This phrase is less formal and less explicit, and although it could be used in many contexts, it might not convey the full intended meaning.
 
• **'A profession of teaching**': This phrase is not suitable because the use of 'a' suggests that teaching is one profession among many, rather than the specific profession being referred to.
 
• '**No improvement**': This option is not applicable because the original phrase "a teaching profession" is not the usual or most accurate way to express the idea.

questions.question:

Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

I. All cups are tables.

II. Some cups are chairs.

I. Some cups are tables.

II. Some tables are chairs.

I. Some cups are tables → It is a definite case, hence true.

II. Some tables are chairs → It is a definite case, hence true.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

’Some’ is a subset of ‘All’. If in statements it is given that ‘All A are B’ then the conclusion ‘Some A are B’ would always be True.

questions.question: What is the value of 6³ + 7³ + 8³ +…… 10³?

Which of the following statement (s) is/are true?

I. 2³⁰⁰ > 3²⁰⁰

II. 6¹⁰⁰ > 2³⁰⁰
questions.solution:
Considering the first statement:

⇒ 2³⁰⁰ > 3²⁰⁰ ⇒ (2³)¹⁰⁰ > (3²)¹⁰⁰

⇒ 8¹⁰⁰ > 9¹⁰⁰

∴ Clearly the above statement is incorrect as 9 is greater than 8.

Considering the second statement:

⇒ 6¹⁰⁰ > 2³⁰⁰ ⇒ 6¹⁰⁰ > 8¹⁰⁰

Again, the above statement is incorrect as 8 is greater than 6.

∴ Neither of the statements are true

questions.question: What is the largest two digit number which is exactly divisible by both 6 and 5?
questions.solution:
We know that the largest two digit number is 99.

If the number is supposed to be divisible by both 5 and 6, then the number is divisible by 5 × 6 = 30.

⇒ 99/30 = (30 × 3) + 9

∴ 99 is not exactly divisible by 30.

∵ 9 is the remainder, we subtract 9 from 99 to get a number exactly divisible by 30.

∴ The largest two-digit number divisible by both 5 and 6 = 99 - 9 = 90

questions.question: If 34P8 is divisible by 9, then what is the value of P?
questions.solution:
If 34P8 is divisible by 9, then the sum of digits is divisible by 9.

⇒ 3 + 4 + P + 8 = 9m

⇒ 15 + P = 9m

⇒ The nearest multiple of 9 is 18

∴ P = 3

questions.question: What is the unit’s digit of 16¹⁰?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

16¹⁰ = 16² × ⁵ ⇒ 256⁵

Here the unit’s digit is the unit digit of the product of 6⁵

⇒ 6 × 6 × 6 × 6 × 6 = 36 × 36 × 6

⇒ 36 × 6 → unit digit is 6.

**∴ Unit digit of 16¹⁰ is 6.**

questions.solution:
Time taken by tap P to fill the tank = 20 minutes

⇒ Part of tank filled in 1 minute = 1/20

Similarly, tank filled by Q and R in 1 min = 1/30 and 1/40 respectively.

⇒ Part of tank filled by all three taps in 1 minute = 1/20 + 1/30 + 1/40 = 13/120

∴ Tank will be completely filled in 120/13 minutes = 9(3)/({13)} minutes

questions.question: Two pipes U and V can fill a cistern in 12 hours and 20 hours respectively. Pipe W can empty the tank in 8 hours. If all the three pipes are opened, then in how many hours the cistern will be full?
questions.solution:
Tank filled by U and V in 1 hour = 1/12 and 1/20 respectively

Tank emptied by W in 1 hour = 1/8

∴ Tank filled by all three in 1 hour = 1/12 + 1/20 - 1/8 = 1/120

∴ Tank will be filled in 120 hours

questions.question: If the surface area of cube is 294 cm², then what is the volume (in cm³) of the cube?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Surface area of cube = 294 cm2

**Formula used:**

Surface area of cube = 6a2

Volume of the cube = a³

Where, 

a → side of the cube.

**Calculation:**

According to the question:

⇒ Surface area of cube = 6a²

⇒ a² = 294/6 = 49

⇒ a = 7 cm

Now,

Volume of the cube = 7³ = 343 cm³

**∴ The volume of the cube is 343 cm3.**

questions.question: Marked price of an article is 35% more than its cost price. If a discount of 40% is given, then what will be the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Let the Cost Price be x

⇒ Marked Price = 1.35x

Now, discount % = 40%

⇒ Selling Price = 1.35x - (0.4 × 1.35x) = 0.81x

∴ Loss % = [(x - 0.81x)/x] × 100 = 19%

questions.question: Selling price of an article is Rs. 6225. If 17% discount is given, then what is the marked price?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The selling price of the article = Rs 6225

Discount = 17%

**Formula used:**

S.P = M.P × (100 - D%)/100

Where,

S.P = Selling price

M.P = Marked price

D = Discount%

**Calculation:**

S.P = M.P × (100 - D%)/100

⇒ 6225 = M.P × (100 - 17)/100

⇒ M.P = (6225 × 100)/(83)

⇒ M.P = 7500

**∴ The marked price of the article is Rs 7500**

questions.question: The ratio of monthly income of Deepak and Raj is 4 : 9 respectively and the ratio of their expenditures is 1 : 3 respectively. If each saves Rs. 9000 per month, then what will be the monthly income (in Rs.) of Deepak?
questions.solution:
Let their monthly incomes be 4x and 9x respectively.

Let their expenditures be y and 3y respectively.

Now, both of them save 9000 every month

4x - y = 9000 and 9x - 3y = 9000

⇒ 4x - y = 9x - 3y

⇒ 5x = 2y

⇒ y = 2.5x

Substituting y’s value in any one of the equations

⇒ 4x - 2.5x = 9000

⇒ 1.5x = 9000

⇒ x = 9000/1.5 = 6000

Deepak’s salary = 4 × 6000 = Rs. 24000

Hence the correct answer is Rs.24000

questions.question: The ratio of four numbers U, V, W, and X is 2 : 7 : 9 : 11 respectively. The sum of V and W is 45 more than the sum of U and X. What is the value of (U + X)?
questions.solution:
Let the numbers be 2x, 7x, 9x and 11x respectively.

⇒ (7x + 9x) = 45 + (2x + 11x)

⇒ 16x = 45 + 13x

⇒ 3x = 45

⇒ x = 45/3 = 15

∴ U + X = 2x + 11x = 30 + 165 = 195

questions.question: Average weight of a group of 11 students is 37 kg. When a student left the group, then average weight of the group becomes 35 kg. What is the weight (in kg) of the student who left?
questions.solution:
⇒ Average weight of 11 students = 37

⇒ Sum of weights of 11 students = 37 × 11 = 407

Now, average weights of 10 students = 35

⇒ Sum of weights of 10 students = 35 × 10 = 350

∴ Weight of the student who left = 407 – 350 = 57 kg

**__ALTERNATE SOLUTION:__**

Weight of student who left = (37 × 11) – 350 = 57

questions.question: If selling price is 60 more than the cost price and profit is 15%, then what is the cost price (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Given:

Selling Price = Rs. 60 more than the cost price

Profit = 15%

Formula used:

C.P = (S.P × 100)/(100 + profit %)

Where, 

C.P = Cost Price

S.P = Selling Price

Calculation:

Let Cost price be Rs. x

According to the question:

Selling Price = Rs. (60 + x)

C.P = ( S.P × 100 )/( 100 + profit %)

⇒ x = [(60 + x) × 100)]/(100 + 15%)

⇒ x = (6000 + 100x)/115

⇒ 115x – 100x = 6000

⇒ 15x = 6000

⇒ x = 6000/15 = Rs. 400

∴ The Cost price is Rs. 400

A train crosses a platform in 45 seconds travelling with a speed of 36 km/h. If the length of the train be 200 metres, then what will be the length (in metres) of the platform?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Speed of the train = 36 km/h

Length of the train = 200 m

Train crosses a platform in 45 seconds

**FORMULA USED:**

Speed = Distance / Time 

**CALCULATION:**

Let the length of platform be ‘x’

⇒ Total distance travelled by train = x + 200

Speed of train = 36km/hr = 10 m/s

Time taken = 45 s

10 = (x + 200)/45

⇒ x + 200 = 450

∴ x = 450 - 200 = 250 m

questions.question: A goes to office at a speed of 10 km/hr and returns home at 40 km/hr. What is his average speed (in km/hr)?
questions.solution:
⇒ Let the distance between home and office be ‘x’

t₁ = x/10

Similarly, t₂ = x/40

Now, Average Speed = Total Distance/total time = 2x/(t₁ + t₂) = 2x/(x/10 + x/40) = 16 km/hr

∴ Average Speed = 16 km/hr

questions.question: A sum amounts to Rs. 2420 in 2 years when invested at compound interest. If principal is Rs. 2000, then what is the rate of interest (in %)?
questions.solution:
Principal Amount = Rs. 2000

Amount = Rs. 2420

Number of years = 2

Amount = P(1 + r/100)t, where P is the principal, r is the rate of interest and t is the time period

2420 = 2000 (1 + r/100)²

1.21 = 1.0201r²

therefore r = sqrt {frac{{1.21}}{{1.0201}}} approx 10\%

questions.question: What are the parallel circles from the equator up to the poles called?
questions.solution:

• Longitudes- Line of references running from North Pole to South Pole. Distance between them is measured in degrees.
 
• Meridian- the half of an imaginary great circle on the Earth's surface, terminated by the North Pole and the South Pole, connecting points of equal longitude

questions.question: Which type of plants have the hard stem branching near the base?
questions.solution:
• Shrubs- small to medium-sized woody plants having persistent woody stems above the ground. Examples- China rose, lemon. 
 
• Herbs- any seed-bearing plant which does not have a woody stem and dies down to the ground after flowering. Examples- Tomato, wheat, grass.
 
• Trees- a perennial plant with an elongated stem or trunk. Trees are big and tall plants. Examples- Banyan, mango, cashew.
